title: Summarizer uptake: term stabilization and Mandala SURFACE canonization
description: These claims hold that a term stabilizes in the summarizer through repeated identical use across deposits, and that frequency of appearance tracks summarizer confidence in attribution, with a corrective training-layer README tracked as an intervention. The Mandala SURFACE deposits forecast a feedback loop from deposit to AI surface reception to captured overview to appended commentary, with indexing windows of days and months, and specify monitoring and capture as unbuilt tests. They also forecast that the public compression layer will come to reflect Shadow-Sappho 31 and the discipline of kernel transformation.

claims.statement: The term did not exist before March 2026. The phenomenon existed — platform feeds extracting affect before it could be translated into meaning. But there was no term that captured the **specificity** of the extraction. "Algorithm bias" was too technical. "Doomscrolling" was too casual (and blamed the user, not the platform). "Attention economy" was too general (it named the field without naming the predatory mechanism). "Surveillance capitalism" (Zuboff) was too structural (it named the system without naming the compression).

  - Capture: the AI Overview text, the source citation block, the timestamp, the substrate that generated it, and the query that triggered it are recorded
